BBC Weather — datePublished and dateModified both 2026-10-25T10:16:20Z = 10:16 GMT Sun 25 Oct (after the cutover, so Z = local). Retrieved by curl at 17:55 GMT. Headline: "More wet and windy weather to follow stormy weekend".

THIS IS THE FORECAST, NOT THE RECORD. Everything below is prospective.

"Storm Boelo will continue to batter parts of the UK on Sunday but the fierce autumn weather shows no sign of clearing quickly. After two named storms in as many days, more wet and potentially very windy weather is forecast to sweep across much of the country on Monday and Tuesday."

"A severe amber wind warning for Storm Boelo remains in force until Sunday evening for much of Scotland and parts of northern England. A second one in Northern Ireland expired on Sunday morning."

THE THIRD SYSTEM — NOT NAMED, NOT CERTAIN
"As the storm clears yet another area of low pressure is expected to move in from the Atlantic, although it remains uncertain whether that system will be strong enough to be named."
"Another area of low pressure is expected to deepen as it approaches the UK from the south-west, bringing a further spell of heavy rain and potentially strong winds to much of the country on Monday and into Tuesday."
"The unsettled weather is set to continue into the start of the week, although conditions should be less severe than those seen across the country since Friday."
"As with Storm Boelo, northern parts of the UK are likely to see the strongest winds and greatest impacts as Tuesday approaches. A yellow warning for wind is in place across Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland and northern England from 03:00 on Tuesday until midnight."
"However, uncertainty remains over the strength and exact track of the developing low-pressure system, meaning the areas likely to experience the most severe conditions could change as the forecast evolves. It is also not yet clear whether the system will be strong enough to be named as another storm."
"Later in the week, the weather looks set to improve for many as high pressure builds over the near continent."

SO, FOR THE RECORD: a third named storm is NOT forecast. A third deep low IS forecast for Monday into Tuesday, and a yellow wind warning for Tuesday 03:00 to midnight has ALREADY been issued for Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland and northern England. Naming is undecided.

CORROBORATION, EARLIER AND WEAKER
BBC Weather's Matt Taylor, in a post on the BBC News live page on Saturday 24 October: "forecasts also show the potential for yet another deep area of low pressure to arrive later on Monday and into Tuesday. It's too early to say if this one will be named, but it looks likely to follow a similar track to Boelo, with the strongest winds focused towards the north of the UK... A fourth storm is looking unlikely though as our weather quietens down through the week." Taylor's Saturday post said the low would follow a track similar to Boelo's; today's article says it approaches from the south-west. Treat the Sunday 10:16 GMT article as the current version.
The Scottish government, in a statement reported by the BBC at 16:49 GMT Sunday, says there is "potential for adverse weather to return in the coming days" and Social Justice and Housing Secretary Shirley-Anne Somerville warns travel disruption is likely to continue into Monday. That is a ministerial restatement, not an independent forecast.
